Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Several week history of left knee pain after fall. Pain localized laterally. No prior surgery.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Mild degenerative subchondral cystic change at the anterior margin of the medial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. 

JOINT SPACE:
Minimal joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Oblique undersurface tear involving the posterior body-horn junction and posterior horn medial meniscus with superimposed small 3 mm intrameniscal cyst formation of the posterior horn. Moderate extrusion of the body partially displaced within the meniscotibial recess.
Medial compartment cartilage: Scattered areas of low grade partial thickness cartilage loss along the central weightbearing medial femoral condyle and along the anterior medial tibial plateau.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the anterior weightbearing lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss involving the lateral patellar facet. Trochlear cartilage remains intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Grade 2 sprain of the fibular collateral ligament proximally near the femoral attachment characterized by high-grade partial-thickness tearing and fiber irregularity and surrounding peritendinous edema. The iliotibial band, biceps femoris and popliteus tendon are intact. Popliteofibular ligament appears intact.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 8 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Moderate prepatellar subcutaneous soft tissue edema and non organized fluid, may reflect underlying soft tissue contusion in the setting of fall. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	High-grade 2 sprain involving the proximal fibular collateral ligament, remaining posterolateral corner structures are intact.
2.	Oblique undersurface tear posterior body and posterior horn medial meniscus with moderate meniscal extrusion and partial displacement within the meniscotibial recess.
3.	Mild tricompartmental chondrosis.
4.	Small Baker cyst.
5.	Moderate anterior soft tissue edema likely representing contusion.

In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The lateral compartment, there is small longitudinal vertical tear at the periphery posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The patellofemoral joint, the patellar and trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 In the intercondylar notch, there is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. There is no tibial translation. 
 The medial collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Some amount of left knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion.  Small longitudinal vertical tear at the periphery posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. 
  Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance.  
  Some amount of left knee effusion.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain for 2 years. No known injury. No history of knee surgery.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Marginal osteophytosis at the patellofemoral compartment. Button osteophyte at the medial femoral condyle.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. Small multiloculated Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Diminutive medial meniscus with blunting of the free edge of the meniscal body. Displaced meniscal fragment to the posterior joint recess. Moderate meniscal extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage irregularity with low-grade cartilage loss at the weightbearing medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade articular cartilage loss throughout the medial patellar facet with regions of full-thickness chondral fissuring at the median ridge. Full-thickness chondral fissuring at the medial and central trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis. Retro-quadriceps fat pad edema. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Mild lateral patellar tilt. No lateral patellar translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 14 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Complex degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus with displaced meniscal fragment at the posterior joint recess.
2.	Moderate patellofemoral compartment and mild medial tibiofemoral compartment chondrosis. 
3.	Small multiloculated Baker's cyst.
4.	Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis.

 The lateral compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury.

 In the intercondylar notch, the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact. There is no tibial translation. 
 The medial collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 No knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion.  Focal cartilage blistering at medial patellar facet (about intact3*intact4 cm).  
  Intact menisci and ligaments of right knee.

Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Intakter Knorpel. Intakter Innenmeniskus. Intaktes MCL.

Laterales Kompartiment:

Kein subchondrales Knochenödem. Mukoide Degeneration des Außenmeniskus am Übergang der Pars intermedia zum Hinterhorn; keine meniskale Rissbildung. Intaktes LCL.

Femoropatellares Gleitlager und Trochlea:

Findings:  No significant knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral articular cartilage is preserved. There is moderate - severe thinning and fraying of the lateral patellar facet articular cartilage with mild underlying bony change. Normal trochlear articular cartilage.  
Conclusion: No meniscal tears. Moderate patellar degenerate change noted.

Conclusion: Mild undersurface degenerate tearing of the posteromedial corner of the medial meniscus. Mild medial compartment articular cartilage thinning.
